Impact Clients is building a new organic growth channel around highly targeted social media pages in the supplement space, each with its own character, audience, voice, and content strategy.
 The goal is simple: create genuinely useful content that earns attention organically, builds trust with specific demographics, and ultimately drives supplement sales through relevant affiliate offers.
 As our AI Creative Strategist , you’ll own the thinking behind the content: developing new characters and avatars, finding angles that resonate with different audiences, writing hooks and scripts, analyzing what performs, and building a repeatable creative system that can scale across dozens of pages.
 This isn’t only a content role.
 What we learn from building this division will eventually become part of the curriculum taught inside our education company. You’ll help train our coaches and students on what’s working while also giving direct product feedback to our engineering team on the AI creative tools you use every day.
 You’ll be helping build the playbook from zero.
 ABOUT IMPACT CLIENTS 
 Impact Clients is a fast-growing tech-enabled education company helping everyday people build online businesses through a combination of education, coaching, community, and proprietary software.
 Our culture is built around clarity, extreme ownership, high standards, and speed of execution .
 We move quickly. We expect people to solve problems without constant direction. And we give talented people a significant amount of ownership when they demonstrate they can produce results.
 If you thrive in environments where creativity and speed go hand-in-hand, where your work gets implemented immediately, and where you're expected to think like an owner rather than an employee, you'll fit in well here.
 This is a fully remote, full-time role. 
 WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU
 A blank canvas. Start from zero and shape the avatars, angles, accounts, and content strategy from the ground up.
 A path to leadership. Help build the team as the channel grows, with the opportunity to eventually lead the creative division.
 A team around you. Work alongside AI video editors and publishing support so your time stays focused on strategy, copy, and creative direction.
 Freedom to test. No ad spend approvals or endless creative bottlenecks. Put ideas into the market, learn what works, and iterate quickly.
 Simple production. Let the strength of the idea carry the content without the heavy production requirements often associated with paid creative.
 Exposure across three business units. Help build a new supplement division, shape how the playbook is taught inside our education business, and influence the roadmap of our proprietary software.
 Real influence beyond your own function. What you discover can become curriculum taught to thousands of students, while your daily use of AI tools helps determine what our engineering team builds next.
 WHAT YOU’RE GETTING INTO - The Day To Day of this Role: 
 Creating the AI avatars: determine which demographics deserve their own character, what those characters should represent, and which concepts should be killed.
 Generate 10–20 new ideas, hooks, and angles every day for short form 7-30 second reels.
 Write and direct scripts for 30–60 second organic Reels , then hand them to the AI video editing team for production.
 Own what gets tested across 5–10+ Instagram and Facebook accounts , each with its own personality, demographic, and content strategy.
 Match message to demographic precisely. A 45-year-old man and a 68-year-old woman should not receive the same hook, framing, or script.
 Turn genuinely useful information into content that earns trust first, allowing the offer in the bio to convert second.
 Study account-level performance and identify which avatars, hooks, formats, and topics are receiving organic distribution.
 Retire weak avatars and scale the characters and concepts that show traction.
 Turn winning creative patterns into repeatable systems rather than one-off successes.
 Help build the department once the model is proven, including future strategists, editors, and publishing support.
 Approximately 10–20% of your time:
 Once the model is proven, help build course content for the company's education division 
 Run a weekly group coaching call helping students apply what we've learned.
 Give our software engineering team hands-on feedback about how to improve the internal AI tools you use every day.
 WHO YOU ARE 
 You come from the direct-response Meta advertising world , ideally within supplements, health, wellness, or another performance-driven ecommerce category.
 You have produced paid creative at meaningful volume — ideally hundreds or thousands of assets per month .
 You are a strong direct-response copywriter, and developing hooks, angles, and concepts is one of your favorite parts of the job.
 You've developed messaging for demographics significantly different from your own.
 You understand that what moves men aged 40–50 may be completely different from what moves women aged 60–70 — and you know how to adjust the creative accordingly.
 You can look at performance data and turn what is working into the next generation of creative ideas.
 You are comfortable testing aggressively, killing losing concepts quickly, and doubling down on winners.
 You are highly fluent with AI creative tools. Our current stack includes Higgsfield, Google Flow Omni, Openart, and CapCut .
 You can operate independently without needing a detailed SOP for every decision.
 Ideally, you've also worked on an info-product, course, or coaching-based offer , particularly in the make-money-online or start-an-online-business space (optional, though preferred).
 The ideal candidate brings an unusual combination: ecommerce/supplement direct-response experience + strong creative strategy and copywriting + familiarity with info-product or coaching businesses. 
 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE In Your First 90 Days On Our Team 
 30 Days: 
Three to five avatars are defined, scripted, and actively in production. A consistent daily idea pipeline exists so the editing team is never waiting on creative direction. The first Reels are live across the initial accounts.
 60 Days: 
We have a clear understanding of which characters, hooks, topics, and angles Instagram and Facebook are actually distributing. Weak avatars are being retired, winning concepts are being expanded across additional accounts, and each audience is matched to a relevant offer.
 90 Days: 
A repeatable system exists from avatar brief → creative concept → script → production → published Reel → performance analysis across 5–10+ accounts, without requiring you to manually touch every step.
 You should also be able to clearly tell us what the department needs next, where the bottlenecks are, and who we need to hire to continue scaling it.
 If this is role is exciting to you, then apply by filling out the questions below. Truly take your time with putting in quality effort into the Loom video, and our team will be in contact with you to schedule interview within 24-48 hours.

Media buying is now the easy part. 
 In 2026, the buying itself is piping. The levers that actually move a DTC account are creative, offer, and conversion rate, and the platform keeps getting better at rewarding whoever gets those right.
 So we don't hire media buyers. We hire marketers who buy media.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands across our service lines, 20 to 25 of them on paid media, and we spend $6-9M a month on Meta. We're hiring one person to own a handful of those accounts end to end.
 Here's what "end to end" actually means here.
 You are the account manager. We don't have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership and accountability: when you're the person answering for the account, it's your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You are the creative strategist. You do the research, you find the angles, and you write the briefs and the scripts. You direct our editors and designers rather than filing requests with them. Creative isn't a ticket you submit. It's your job.
 You build the things the account needs. If conversion rate is the bottleneck, you build the landing page. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You carry up to six accounts. That's the capacity we run at today, and the team averages about four and a half. You'll manage far fewer accounts than you would at most agencies. In exchange you get real ownership of the results and you get to work as an end to end marketer instead of one station on an assembly line.
 You can live anywhere. We're a remote team and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you're the client's point of contact and there's nobody else to cover it. The rest of your day is yours.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we'll both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 We're growing fast and we keep the bar high. 
 We believe the best media buyer today is a sharp marketer who uses AI every day. We built an internal creative analysis tool that connects to Claude, and we use Pipeboard to read and write to ad accounts and run heavy analysis. You don't need to know our stack yet. You do need to actually use AI in your work, not be afraid of it, and teach yourself what you don't know.
 What the job looks like
 Own 4 to 6 DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, the creative lead, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $30k/mo to $1M/mo.
 Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you're the one who answers when something isn't working.
 Run the research before the ads. Marketing is 80% research here. You mine customer reviews, ad comments, support tickets, and Reddit for the language and objections that become angles. You pull competitor ad libraries. You run our internal tooling that OCRs and transcribes the ads in your account and ties them to performance, so you know what winning and losing actually look like in this account.
 Write the briefs and the scripts, and direct the work. Creative direction is yours. You run revision rounds with our editors and designers and you hold the quality bar.
 Ship creative on a cadence. Roughly 8 to 10 new ad launches a week is where accounts hold, in batches every 1 to 1.5 weeks. Informed volume, not spray and pray. We want better hypotheses, not more randomness.
 Build and test landing pages. Advertorials, comparison pages, PDPs. Built in Claude Code, deployed to Vercel, tested live on a subdomain before anything gets pushed into the client's theme.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Report on new customer economics. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended ROAS and not last click. You'll be expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.
 You're a fit if
 You've done this with real money. Hands-on Meta at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them.
 You're AI-native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude (or equivalent) as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it. If you can research, write, and build a converting page from scratch, we can teach you the buying.
 You can write direct response in English at a native or near-native level. Hooks, scripts, ad copy, advertorial. In the customer's own words, not invented. This is the single biggest source of leverage in the role and the thing we screen hardest for. If writing persuasive English isn't a strength, this isn't the job.
 You can communicate your ideas. This matters as much as anything else on this list. You'll be in front of clients constantly with nobody in between, so you need to be able to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire.
 You have taste and you know when to hand off. You direct creative, you don't half-build it yourself. AI slop shipped to a client is a habit we break, not a shortcut we accept.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you've built or operated your own Shopify store or eComm brand. Several of our team have, and it shows.
 You're not a fit if
 "That wasn't my role" is in your vocabulary. It's the fastest way to end an interview here. If creative was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the creative.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 Why This Role Is Exciting
 This is not a maintenance job. You will be surrounded by people who move fast, care a lot, and take the work seriously.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets.  We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You will grow into senior strategy.  We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 An overview of this role 
 Site Reliability Engineers keep GitLab's user-facing services and production systems running reliably at scale. They combine software engineering with operational excellence, applying sound engineering principles, automation, and continuous improvement to build, operate, and evolve our production infrastructure.
 This is a single application for Site Reliability Engineering opportunities across Infrastructure Platforms. Rather than asking you to choose the right team or level upfront, we evaluate your skills holistically and match you to the opportunity that best aligns with your experience and our hiring needs. We hire Site Reliability Engineers from Intermediate through Senior Staff across multiple Infrastructure Platforms teams.
 We don't expect every candidate to have experience with every technology in our environment. We're looking for engineers with strong technical fundamentals, a growth mindset, and the ability to learn quickly. We'll support you in becoming successful with GitLab's tools, systems, and ways of working.
 Please note: This position is open to candidates based in the United States and Canada only. Candidates based in the United Kingdom can apply to this posting: Site Reliability Engineer, Infrastructure Platforms — UK (Intermediate to Senior Staff) 
 How our SRE hiring works 
 Because this is a single application for SRE roles across Infrastructure Platforms, our process is built to evaluate you once and match you well, rather than interviewing separately for every team.
 Recruiter Screen: A conversation about your background, what you're looking for, and the level and teams that fit, so we can point your process in the right direction.
 Core Technical: The shared assessment every SRE candidate takes, regardless of eventual team. A low-stress, collaborative discussion covering system architecture and incident review.
 Hiring Manager Interview: A conversation about ownership, judgment, execution, collaboration, and growth, the non-technical signals that make an SRE effective at GitLab.
 Peer Technical: Team-specific depth, run by SREs from the team you're most likely to join, focused on the problems that team actually works on.
 Skip-Level Interview: A conversation with a senior leader on values alignment, and how you'll work across teams.
 After your interviews, we consider your performance alongside our current hiring needs to confirm the level and team where you'll do your best work. Interview results are a major factor, and final placement also reflects our active hiring priorities at the time.
 We’ll calibrate your level throughout the interview process based on the scope and impact of your experience. 
 Intermediate: You independently deliver meaningful reliability improvements within a defined area.
 Senior: You own complex reliability work end to end and raise the effectiveness of your team.
 Staff: You shape reliability across multiple teams, solving systemic problems and creating approaches others can reuse.
 Senior Staff: You set technical direction across a broader Infrastructure area and influence reliability strategy at organizational scale.
 What you'll do

 Build automation and tooling that reduces toil and replaces manual work with repeatable, infrastructure-as-code-driven workflows
 Operate and troubleshoot production systems on Kubernetes, including deployments, rollouts, and scaling
 Write and maintain infrastructure as code, and ship changes safely through CI/CD and GitOps
 Participate in on-call, triage alerts, follow and improve runbooks, and escalate appropriately
 Contribute to the observability stack, using metrics, logs, and SLOs to detect symptoms early rather than just outages
 Take part in incident response and post-incident reviews, turning learnings into changes in automation and process
 Document runbooks, architecture decisions, and reviews so your findings become repeatable practices
 What you'll bring 
 Experience keeping production systems reliable, combining an operations mindset with real software engineering practice
 Experience building net-new infrastructure tooling and automation, not just configuring existing tools. For example, Terraform modules, Kubernetes operators or controllers, or production automation and services written from scratch

This includes sorting, washing, drying, folding, and properly tracking all laundry while maintaining hygiene, safety, and cross-contamination prevention protocols. The Laundry Attendant works closely with the housekeeping team to support the daily operations of the lodge.
 This position requires fly-in/fly-out travel from Edmonton, Alberta or Yellowknife, Northwest Territories to the project site in Nunavut, with potential for weather-related delays or logistical challenges. Employees are responsible for arranging their own transportation to the designated point of dispatch.

 Collect, count, weigh, and log all personal laundry using tracking sheets/ program.
 Assist housekeepers and guests with personal laundry bag drop-off and pick-up.
 Secure small personal laundry bags with zip ties; combine multiple small bags in large machines to save water and time.
 Pick up personal laundry during scheduled night shift times (e.g., 7:00 pm and 9:00 pm).
 Ensure timely processing: all personal laundry washed by 12:30–1:00 pm, dried by 4:00 pm.
 Prioritize certain clients, ensuring return of laundry before required times (e.g., 2:00 pm).
 Keep washers and dryers running continuously; avoid idle machines.
 Run additional spin cycles on small stacking washers to ensure proper drying.

 To launder clothing, other washable materials, and use only the instructed washers and dryers for them.

 Employees are responsible for arranging their transportation to the designated point of dispatch (typically Edmonton, Alberta).
 Fly-in/fly-out position based in a remote Arctic camp, with potential for weather-related travel delays.

THE ROLE

We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Foundations team, which is responsible for the systems, patterns, and surfaces that help us build consistent, high-quality experiences. You’ll play a key role in shaping and evolving UI components and UX patterns in Jobber’s design system across multiple platforms. This role necessarily involves thinking about how the design system operates in an evolving age of AI design and development. You’ll lead projects and initiatives that raise standards for visual and interaction design, usability, and accessibility, while improving consistency and team velocity.

Our team collaborates closely with designers, product managers, and engineers across the company. You’ll work at the intersection of design, engineering, and systems thinking to help other teams build better experiences, faster, and to turn good ideas into great experiences that are easier to build, ship, and repeat.

 - Lead design system projects to create and refine components, interaction patterns, and design tokens that scale across web and mobile platforms

 - Apply Jobber’s brand and experience principles to the product through thoughtful, high-quality visual and interaction design

 - Identify gaps in the system and proactively drive solutions that improve consistency and usability at scale, and raise the bar for UX quality

 - Define and evolve governance models, contribution processes, and best practices

 - Partner closely with Engineering to ensure high-quality implementation and to improve how we incorporate the system into AI-backed design and development tools and workflows

 - Collaborate with designers and product teams to support adoption, share best practices, and incorporate feedback

 - Advocate for UX quality across the company to improve visual design, interaction design, accessibility, usability, and performance

 - Contribute to a strong culture of collaboration, mentorship, feedback, and continuous improvement

 - 2–5 years experience designing and evolving design systems, including work on components, patterns, tokens, and documentation

 - A track record of leading projects or initiatives that improved design consistency and quality across a product

 - Deep expertise in interaction design, UI patterns, and visual design

 - Strong understanding of accessibility standards for the web and/or mobile and how to embed them into systems

 - Comfort collaborating closely with engineers and understanding how design translates to code

 - Familiarity with front-end technologies (HTML, CSS, and frameworks like React)

 - Strong proficiency in today’s evolving AI design landscape, including prototyping, shared libraries, and design documentation

About KidKare 
 The people who care for and feed children every day have enough on their plates. Their software shouldn't add to it. 
 For more than 30 years, KidKare has built technology for the people behind childcare and child nutrition, helping them spend less time on paperwork, compliance, and administrative work and more time focused on the children and communities they serve.
 Our roots run deep in the Child and Adult Care Food Program (CACFP), a federal nutrition program that helps provide healthy meals and snacks to children and adults across the country. Today, we're building on that expertise with a growing ecosystem of software supporting childcare organizations across food program compliance, business management, professional development, and licensing.
 We have a much bigger vision for what we can do across the childcare community with a strong plan focused on bringing more value to customers through new features, modules, and products. To support these goals, we're looking for an AI Engineer to embed within one of our mature, deeply configurable platforms that has real functional and technical complexity built up over years of customer-driven development.
 Position Summary 
 You'll be working inside a legacy codebase with established architecture, business rules, and customer commitments, and your job is twofold:  
 (1) use AI tooling to extend and modernize what these platforms can do, and  
 (2) use that same AI expertise to make our existing engineering teams faster and sharper — compressing the time between a customer requirement and a shipped, correct solution. 
 You will work directly with engineering leads, product, and operators to find where AI-assisted development — code generation, automated testing, requirement-to-implementation acceleration, intelligent tooling — can shorten delivery cycles without sacrificing quality, especially under aggressive customer timelines. 
 If you enjoy going deep into complex, configurable systems and making both the product and the team around it faster, this role is for you. 
 Your mission: use AI to multiply the output and accuracy of our development teams, while extending the intelligence of the platforms themselves. 
 Primary Responsibilities 
 Accelerate team delivery 
 ·        Introduce and operationalize AI-assisted development practices (code generation, AI pair-programming, automated test generation) across existing engineering teams. 
 ·        Identify friction points in how requirements move from customer ask to shipped feature, and apply AI tooling to close the gap. 
 ·        Partner with developers working in Angular, React, C#, and TypeScript to embed AI tooling into their actual day-to-day workflow — not a side project. 
 ·        Build reusable patterns/playbooks so AI-assisted delivery scales across teams, not just your own output. 
 Extend platform intelligence 
 ·        Design, develop, and deploy AI features directly into existing, deeply configurable SaaS platforms. 
 ·        Integrate LLMs and ML models into legacy architectures without destabilizing existing functional/technical requirements. 
 ·        Build automation pipelines that reduce manual operational tasks within the product and internally. 
 ·        Develop intelligent agents and AI-powered workflow systems where they create measurable leverage. 
 Architect AI Infrastructure 
 ·        Implement RAG systems and embedding pipelines. 
 ·        Work with vector databases and retrieval systems. 
 ·        Build AI orchestration layers and agent frameworks. 
 ·        Ensure reliability, monitoring, and evaluation of AI outputs. 
 ·        Deploy and maintain models in production environments. 
 Collaborate cross-functionally 
 ·        Work directly with engineering leads and non-technical stakeholders to understand both platform constraints and business pain points. 
 ·        Translate ambiguous problems — in the product or in the development process — into scalable AI solutions. 
 ·        Balance speed with engineering rigor, especially against aggressive customer-driven timelines. 
 ·        Drive execution with minimal oversight. 
 Required Technical Skills 
 Core engineering 
 ·        Experience working within deeply configurable, enterprise-grade SaaS platforms (not greenfield products). 
 ·        Strong Python expertise (required). 
 ·        Comfortable across multiple languages/frameworks — Angular, React, C#, and TypeScript. 
 ·        Backend development experience (APIs, microservices) in a mature production codebase. 
 ·        Experience deploying production systems; familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP). 
 ·        CI/CD, Docker, containerization. 
 AI & ML systems 
 Experience with: 
 ·        LLM integration (OpenAI, Anthropic, open-source models, etc.) 
 ·        AI-assisted development tooling (code generation / coding copilots, applied at team scale, not just individually)

 Familiarity with:

 Data & automation 
 Experience with:

 ·        API integrations across SaaS platforms. 
 ·        Automation tooling and workflow orchestration. 
 MLOps & productionization 
 Experience with:

 Monitoring model performance. 
 Logging and observability. 
 A/B testing AI features. 
 You'll Probably Love This Role If…

We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients. 
 At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute. 
 To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com 
 What you'll be doing 
 Our AI team builds enterprise capabilities that support a wide range of users across the organization, from end users to technology teams and low-code or no-code builders. As a Principal Product Scaler – AI Engineering, you'll build the engineering foundation that helps us repeatedly deliver high-quality AI products safely, efficiently, and at scale. You'll architect and develop the reusable components, software development kits, testing frameworks, and delivery patterns that move us from individual implementations to a mature product engineering model. You'll establish the standards for how AI products are designed, built, tested, packaged, released, and monitored in production. Working closely with data scientists, engineers, and technology partners, you'll help turn strong prototypes into reliable enterprise products while strengthening the team's overall engineering capability.
 At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. Details on your work arrangement (proportion of on-site and remote work) will be discussed at the time of your interview. 
 How you'll succeed 
 Build scalable engineering foundations - Design and develop software development kits, libraries, reusable components, templates, and reference implementations that accelerate delivery across the AI portfolio and reduce repeated effort across teams.
 Establish engineering excellence - Define and implement standards for code structure, testing, code review, versioning, packaging, documentation, release management, and production readiness for AI and Generative AI products.
 Advance AI quality and reliability - Create automated testing, evaluation, regression, monitoring, and observability patterns that support both traditional software quality and the unique behavior of probabilistic AI systems.
 Drive efficient delivery - Establish continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) patterns, quality gates, and repeatable workflows that help teams move from experiment to production with greater speed and consistency.
 Enable adoption across teams - Design interfaces and developer experiences that make enterprise AI capabilities easy to consume for technology teams, other AI teams, and low-code or no-code solution builders.
 Elevate team capability - Review architecture and code for critical products, coach AI practitioners on engineering best practices, and help the team adopt effective agentic development workflows, tooling, and guardrails.
 Who you are 
 You are a hands-on senior engineering leader . You have atleast 5+ experience operating at a Staff, Principal, Lead Engineer, or equivalent level, and you enjoy both designing systems and writing production-quality code.

It’s an asset if you have built platforms, frameworks, developer tooling, or reusable services used by multiple teams.
 You give meaning to data . You understand the engineering challenges of taking AI and Generative AI solutions from experimentation into production, and you know that quality for AI systems requires more than traditional unit testing.
 You look beyond the moment. You're excited by the opportunity to shape how agentic software development evolves, including workflows, repository design, testing approaches, review practices, context management, and governance for increasingly autonomous delivery.
 You're motivated by collective success . You influence engineers, data scientists, technology partners, and leaders through strong partnership, sound judgment, and a commitment to raising the capability of the broader organization.
 You act like an owner . You naturally identify repeated patterns, remove friction from the development lifecycle, and build practical solutions that help teams deliver faster, more safely, and with greater consistency.
 You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

 This role sits at the centre of the business and spans the functions that set our direction: corporate strategy, finance and planning, business operations, corporate development, and go-to-market. In a single quarter that might mean owning the operating model, running a pricing analysis, sizing a new market, preparing the board package, and driving a diligence work stream.
 What separates it from a traditional strategy and operations seat is how the work gets done. This is an AI-native role by design. The models, agents and automated workflows behind planning, reporting and analysis are yours to build, deploy and maintain, and the systems you put in place become how the rest of the company operates.
 You will have direct line of sight to the executive team and to the decisions that shape the company, along with real latitude to decide where your time creates the most value.
 This is a Hybrid role based in Toronto (Harbourfront Centre), with regular in-person time alongside the team.
 What You'll Do
 Partner directly with the executive team to translate strategy into operating plans, tracking execution across functions and unblocking what slows us down. Where a priority has no natural owner, you pick it up and carry it to a decision.
 Own the strategy and the analysis behind our hardest questions, from market entry and pricing through to unit economics, headcount planning and capital allocation. Frame the problem, build the model, and bring a recommendation with a number behind it.
 Own business operations across the company. Design and run the processes, systems and reporting that connect product, go-to-market, engineering and internal operations, including the vendor and partner relationships that support them, and strengthen that foundation as the business scales.
 Define where AI belongs in how the business runs. Map how work actually gets done today across product, go-to-market, finance and operations, and separate the places where AI creates real leverage from the places where it is only novelty.
 Lead adoption across the organization. Partner with function leads to redesign how work is structured rather than layering new tools onto existing processes, and manage the transition so that changes are embedded and sustained.  3 to 7 years in strategy and operations, business operations, chief of staff, corporate finance, or another broad cross-functional role.  Advanced, hands-on AI fluency. You are current by default: when something meaningful ships, you have usually already tried it.
 Quantitative depth. You are comfortable in a model and with a blank spreadsheet, and you can move between a P&L, a cohort curve and a pricing scenario without friction.
 First-principles thinking. You take a problem apart from scratch rather than pattern-matching to the last place you worked.
 Writing that moves decisions. You can turn a messy situation into a clear one-pager that gets a call made.
 Comfort with breadth. You are energised by variety, and by not knowing exactly what you will own next quarter.
 Ownership instinct. You move without waiting to be told, and you close loops.

 Consumer technology, mobile, ad tech, platforms, gaming or interactive entertainment experience.

 Access to leading AI tools and platforms
